clue.text: After a job

definitions.meaning: the Latin-derived prefix meaning after, as in postwar
a position of employment

explanation.definitionFit: Post- means later as a prefix, and a post is also a paid position or appointment.

clue.text: Surface pollution total is about a hundred

indicators.note: is about means one word goes around another, so the sum wraps the letter

parts.note: a total is a sum
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A count of a pollutant is put at roughly a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts C, the Roman hundred, inside SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is the film of dirt or froth that floats on top of a liquid.

clue.text: Give out just when it is time to got back

indicators.note: to go back means the word time is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone gives up just at the moment they should return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' turns TIME round; 'just when it is' is padding to make the surface read.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit something is to send or discharge it outwards.

clue.text: Murder detective's first question to no one in particular

definitions.meaning: a detective arriving at a murder scene might first ask whether there is a corpse
whichever person at all, unspecified

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word asks whether a corpse is present; whole, it means whoever, any person at all.

clue.text: Much the same colours presented for a hard fought game

definitions.meaning: two shades nearly identical are a near likeness
a contest decided by a narrow margin

explanation.definitionFit: Colours that nearly correspond are a near likeness; a narrowly contested game is also a tight contest.

clue.text: Plea by reluctant lender is an explosive bloomer

definitions.meaning: to touch someone is to borrow money from them, so a reluctant lender begs not to be touched
the impatiens plant of that name has seed pods that burst open when ripe

explanation.definitionFit: The flower Impatiens noli-tangere has pods that burst when brushed, and the phrase is also a plea not to be asked for a loan.

clue.text: Cry stinking fish when the starter's flag falls?

definitions.text: Cry stinking fish when the starter's flag falls?

parts.words: Cry stinking fish when the starter's flag falls?
parts.note: a remark that fish have gone bad doubles as the commentator's shout as a race begins

explanation.definitionFit: Racing commentators shout this phrase as the horses leave the start, and it also says that some food has spoiled.

clue.text: Bitterness robs the Bible of its heart

indicators.note: robs signals that a letter is taken away from the book
its heart is the middle letter of the five-letter book name

parts.note: taken as written, the holy book

explanation.surface: Bitter feeling strips scripture of its core meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: BIBLE has five letters, so its heart is the third, B; removing it leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bile, the digestive fluid, figuratively means bitter anger or resentment.

clue.text: Hook an early heretic from an uncivilised land

parts.note: a barb is the backward-pointing hook on an arrow or fish-hook
an Arian followed Arius, whose fourth-century teaching was condemned as heresy

explanation.surface: A hooked weapon is linked with an early church heretic from wild country.
explanation.walkthrough: Arius was a 4th-century priest whose views on the Trinity the early Church condemned.
explanation.definitionFit: To the Greeks and Romans, a barbarian was a foreigner from outside their civilised world.

clue.text: Schedule provided by a pedestal sundial?

definitions.meaning: a list of times for trains, classes and so on
a sundial on a stand is literally a table that tells the hour

explanation.definitionFit: A schedule of departures is a timetable; a sundial on a pedestal is whimsically a table showing the hour.

clue.text: English City newspaper called The Salamander

parts.note: the FT, Financial Times, is the newspaper of the City of London financial district

explanation.surface: A London financial paper gives an amphibian a name.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, and the Financial Times is its paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, a small amphibian of the salamander family.

clue.text: Crusty bread from a flower in South Wales

annotationWithheld.why: Crusty bread from a flower in South Wales: the river USK gives USK, but no clue word supplies the R, so the clue looks garbled as held
annotationWithheld.clue: Crusty bread from a flower in South Wales

clue.text: Boy turns delinquent

indicators.note: turns means the word boy is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' sends BOY backwards; the surface reads as a boy turning to crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A yob is a rowdy, loutish young man, the British slang word for a hooligan.

clue.text: Request for 640 gallons taken just before closing time

parts.note: a last is an old unit of capacity, here 640 gallons
an order is a request for goods or drinks

explanation.surface: Someone asks for an enormous quantity of drink just before a pub shuts.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is an old British trade measure; for liquid it was 640 gallons.
explanation.definitionFit: In a British pub the barman calls for final drink requests shortly before closing.

clue.text: Landlord has a stake in mailing charge

parts.note: a letter is one who lets property
a post is a stake driven into the ground

explanation.surface: A landlord has invested in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has a stake' looks like having a financial interest, but the stake is a wooden POST.
explanation.definitionFit: Letter post is the postal rate for sending letters as opposed to parcels.

clue.text: Woman had a rip in her dress and sobbed

parts.note: she refers to a woman
a tear is a rip in cloth

explanation.surface: A woman tore her dress and wept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' is read as a rip, but the answer reads the same letters as a drop from the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed a tear is to weep, an idiom for crying.

clue.text: Outdoor tennis ground where judges admit the public

definitions.meaning: a tennis surface in the open air
a court session that spectators may attend

explanation.definitionFit: A tennis court without a roof is open, and a hearing anyone may watch is held openly.

clue.text: The purposes of first rate writing

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written AI, the figure 1 standing for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aims are goals or intentions.

clue.text: Said to have circulated forged notes

definitions.meaning: spoke or voiced
uttering is the legal term for passing counterfeit money

explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to speak, and in law to utter is to put forged money into circulation.

clue.text: Oil refinery in Gath supplies its mightiest son

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the town name

parts.note: taken as written, the Philistine city

indicators.note: a refinery processes crude, so the letters of oil are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An oil refinery in the ancient city supplies its greatest son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refinery' makes OLI from OIL, and 'in' puts it inside GATH after the G. Goliath came from Gath in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath, the giant slain by David, was a champion from Gath.

clue.text: Who knows the answer to a highwayman's threat?

definitions.meaning: a teacher asking which pupils can respond
a robber orders victims to raise their arms

explanation.definitionFit: A teacher asks pupils to raise an arm if they can respond, and a robber orders surrender the same way.

clue.text: To her is given a name fit for a heavenly queen

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman is given a name worthy of a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: HER plus A gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera was queen of the Greek gods on Olympus, wife of Zeus.

clue.text: Cut straw 2.54 cm long for a songbird

parts.note: chaff is chopped straw or husks
an inch is 2.54 centimetres

explanation.surface: Measuring chopped straw for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch.

clue.text: One with a 50/50 chance of recovery?

definitions.text: One with a 50/50 chance of recovery?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
L is the Roman numeral fifty, twice

explanation.surface: A patient whose odds of getting better are even.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a sick person may or may not recover.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unwell is a person whose recovery is uncertain.

clue.text: Return of the oat to the Chinese path

indicators.note: Return of means the word oat is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Grain coming back along a road in China.
explanation.definitionFit: Tao, in Chinese philosophy, is the Way, the path of nature.

clue.text: Church recess called by a brief addition to a note

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a short addition to a letter
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A church alcove given a short postscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' plays on a letter with a PS, but E is the musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the vaulted semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Emphasize importance of tube railway route

definitions.meaning: to stress
an underground track runs beneath the surface

explanation.definitionFit: To stress something is to put a line beneath it; a line beneath the streets is a tube route.

clue.text: Teases wool into a raised rows of knitting

definitions.meaning: makes fun of
a knitted pattern of ridges

explanation.definitionFit: To rib someone is to tease them, and ribs are ridged lines in knitwear.

clue.text: Edge one's way cautiously in church

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the standard abbreviation for church; that the letters also run on in the printed words is a coincidence, not a hidden word

explanation.walkthrough: CH is a common short form of church.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward is to move slowly by small degrees.

clue.text: They look and sound as if they agree

indicators.note: sound as if means the letters are chosen because they are said like another word

parts.note: ayes are votes in favour

explanation.surface: People who look and seem to be agreeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ayes' are yes votes in Parliament, pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes are the organs of sight.

clue.text: Former enemy of American navy vessel right to the end

parts.note: USS, United States Ship, prefixes American navy vessel names

explanation.surface: A one-time foe of the US Navy fought to the last.
explanation.walkthrough: The R goes last, as 'to the end' says; USS is the prefix of US Navy ship names.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet Union was America's Cold War adversary.

clue.text: A handy adjuster for a torture instrument

definitions.meaning: a screw turned by hand
a device crushing the digits

explanation.definitionFit: A screw with a winged head is turned by fingers; it is also an old device for crushing fingers.
